model: VULCAN-2D full-cycle link with a protocol-conditioned RESET HRS attractor

rejected_cycles.reason: RESET cycle does not have separable LRS and HRS envelopes
RESET cycle does not have separable LRS and HRS envelopes

prediction_protocol.target_inputs: target S_i voltage/current and target R_i voltage protocol; target R_i current is used only for quality control, labels and scoring
prediction_protocol.validation: leave-one-cycle-out: each S_i-to-RESET-state law excludes the target R_i starting-state label
prediction_protocol.reset_law_training: transport and transition-field laws use only the 0.9-V and 1.3-V RESET ensembles; the legacy HRS/LRS gate-ratio law is retained only as a comparator

set_reset_transfer.feature_interpretation: voltage-domain exposure proxy; proportional to charge only under a common linear ramp rate

reset_endpoint_diagnosis.diagnosis: At fixed gate and protocol, HRS is substantially more concentrated than LRS and is not positively correlated with LRS; a fixed HRS/LRS ratio transfers spurious LRS variance into the RESET return branch.

protocol_conditioned_hrs_attractor.protocol: paired 0 to -1.7 to 0 V DC RESET
protocol_conditioned_hrs_attractor.validation: leave-one-cycle-out; each target endpoint is predicted from the other 50 accepted cycles

endpoint_model_selection.decision: Selected the protocol attractor: it is simpler than an additional SET-to-HRS slope and gives the lowest terminal RESET return-branch error.

chronological_endpoint_check.interpretation: The later cycles shift to a higher HRS conductance than the first 35. The attractor still improves the later median return curve, but its individual endpoint error reveals cycle-order drift that a stationary distribution cannot explain.

claim_scope.paired_order: S_i is the measured operation immediately before R_i
claim_scope.reset_target_leakage: target RESET current is not a model input
claim_scope.set_exposure: integral |I| dV is a voltage-domain proxy; without sweep time it is not an absolute charge or energy
claim_scope.physical_interpretation: SET history contains statistical information about the following RESET starting conductance; correlation does not identify a unique atomistic migration species
claim_scope.hrs_endpoint: within a fixed gate and DC protocol, final HRS is represented by a log-domain attractor distribution rather than a fixed HRS/LRS ratio
claim_scope.hrs_endpoint_generalization: the attractor may be used only at its fitted gate and protocol; cross-gate changes can include batch effects
claim_scope.remaining_limit: the SET trace is experimental input, so this is a measured-SET-conditioned full cycle, not a fully autonomous SET simulator

verdict.interpretation: The measured SET history weakly but significantly improves the following RESET starting conductance. At the fixed 1.1-V gate and DC protocol, RESET ends near a narrower HRS distribution rather than preserving a fixed HRS/LRS ratio. Neither relation identifies a microscopic species.
